# THE LAST RAIL — Implementation progress

## Version 1.0 — App Store release preparation (2026-10-13)

See `APP_STORE_RELEASE.md` (step-by-step guide), `RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md` (status) and `AppStore/` (metadata, privacy, screenshots).

* Version 1.0 (build 1), development language Swedish, `ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption = NO`, `UIUserInterfaceStyle = Dark` (dark launch screen), `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` added.
* New opaque app icon of Lok 7, generated by `Tools/AppIcon/makeicon.swift`.
* Placeholder texts removed (wagon "Ej i version 0.2" tiles, "kommande/framtida version" texts). The main menu shows the bundle version.
* Story texts reflowed. Long dialogs flash their scroll indicator.
* Debug tools (`-TLRScenario`, `-TLRFreshStart`, new `-TLRShowFPS`, new scenario token `routes`) are compiled out of Release.
* 74/74 tests pass on iPhone SE (3rd gen), 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max simulators. Simulator performance: 60 FPS, about 5% CPU, about 128 MB with flat memory over 60 scene transitions.
* Release archive builds and is development-signed. App Store export is blocked until the owner enrolls in the paid Apple Developer Program.

---

**Version 0.2: native iPhone game, landscape only.** Swift, SwiftUI and SpriteKit, iOS 17 or later.
All in-game text is in Swedish. There are no external assets, no network access and no dependencies.

Version 0.1 was mistakenly built for macOS. 0.2 converts the whole game to iOS. Game rules, content, progression, save format and pixel art are unchanged; the platform layer (input, view hosting, lifecycle) and the entire UI were redone for a touchscreen.

## Platform status

| Item | Status |
|---|---|
| Deployment target | iOS 17.0, iPhone only (`TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = 1`) |
| Orientation | Landscape Left + Landscape Right only (`UISupportedInterfaceOrientations_iPhone`), `UIRequiresFullScreen`, status bar hidden, home indicator auto-hidden |
| Safe areas | World rendering fills the whole screen. HUD and panels stay inside the safe area (Dynamic Island / notch / home indicator). |
| Screen sizes | The logical world viewport is 270 px high, with its width set from the device's aspect ratio. Verified on iPhone 17 Pro (Dynamic Island) and iPhone SE 3rd gen (667×375, the smallest). |
| Frame rate | `SKView.preferredFramesPerSecond = 60`; exploration maps are baked into single textures |
| Saving | JSON in the app sandbox: `Library/Application Support/TheLastRail/` (`save.json`, `save.backup.json`, `settings.json`). Autosaves when the app goes to the background. |
| Audio | `AVAudioSession` category `.ambient`, which mixes with other audio and respects the silent switch. The engine restarts when the app becomes active after an interruption. |
| Haptics | Light feedback on taps and pickups, success on crafting/repair/secrets, error on faint or failure |
| macOS remnants | Removed: AppKit, keyboard monitor, mouse/scroll handlers, window/fullscreen code, the "Avsluta" (Quit) button, and the macOS snapshot harness |

## How to build and run

`xcode-select` on this Mac points to the Command Line Tools, so command-line builds need `DEVELOPER_DIR`:

```bash
export DEVELOPER_DIR=/Volumes/WD-BLACK/User/Apps/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer
xcodebuild -project "The Last Rail.xcodeproj" -scheme "The Last Rail" -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17 Pro' build
xcodebuild test -project "The Last Rail.xcodeproj" -scheme "The Last Rail" -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17 Pro'
```

* In Xcode: open the project, pick an iPhone simulator or your device, then Run.
* To run on a physical iPhone, choose your team under Signing & Capabilities. Automatic signing is set up with team `B8SM9PP3KC`; no signing certificate is installed on this Mac.

### Debug scenarios (simulator verification)

`-TLRScenario "<tokens>"` jumps straight into a game state, using a throwaway save folder. Example:

```bash
xcrun simctl launch <device> Victor-Svensson.The-Last-Rail -TLRScenario "skip;wagons;train:nordpasset;overlay:map"
```

Tokens: `newgame`, `skip`, `explore:<station>[@col,row]`, `at:col,row`, `train:<station>`, `wagons`, `lamp`, `travel:<station>`, `overlay:<map|crafting|inventory|journal|wagons|locomotive|pause|settings|help|repair|complete|keypad>`, `dialog`.

`-TLRFreshStart` deletes the real save first; the UI tests use it.

## Touch controls

### Exploration
* **Floating joystick:** put a thumb anywhere on the left half of the screen, below the HUD. The stick is analog: speed follows how far you drag.
* **Action button** (hand, bottom right): plays the role of the old E key. It glows when something is in reach, and the current action ("Plocka upp järnskrot", "Gå ombord på tåget", …) is shown just above it.
* **Sprint button** (runner, next to the action button): hold it.
* **Simultaneous input:** one UIKit view (`TouchControlsView`) tracks every finger separately through `TouchControlModel`. Moving, sprinting and the action button all work at once. A second finger in the joystick zone is ignored. Controls are released automatically when a panel or dialog opens.
* **Top-right buttons:** Ryggsäck, Karta (greyed out until the map is unlocked), Journal, Paus.
* **Top left:** a small status card with health, backpack fill and carried resources.
* **Objective tracker:** collapses with a tap so it never has to cover the world.
* **Camera:** follows the player smoothly at a closer zoom (0.8×) than on the Mac, so the character reads well on a phone.

### Train
* Swipe horizontally to move along the train. Pinch to zoom.
* Tap the locomotive for the locomotive panel. Tap a cargo wagon for storage, or crafting if it has a workbench. Tap the living wagon to rest.
* **Bottom bar** (44 pt icon buttons): Karta, Lager, Bygg, Vagnar, Loket, Journal, Kliv av.
* Large status card: fuel, storage, condition and weight.
* **Travel panel:** progress, fast-forward and skip.

### Railway map
* Drag to pan, pinch to zoom (1–3×), and a "Återställ" button resets the view. Tap a station to inspect it.
* The info column shows distance, fuel estimate, travel time and requirements.
* A pinned action button is always visible: **Res hit**, **Tanka och res** or **Nödkörning**.
* Station tap targets that are zoomed outside the visible map are hidden, because SwiftUI clipping does not stop hit-testing. A UI test found this bug.

### Panels (all redesigned for a landscape phone)
* Full-screen panels with a 44 pt close button. Most use two- or three-column layouts that fit an iPhone SE without scrolling.
* Only long lists scroll: recipes, journal text, help.
* Panels:
  * Inventory: backpack, train storage, health/eat and tools in columns;
  * Crafting: recipe list, detail and a large Build button;
  * Locomotive: big refuel tiles;
  * Wagons: reorder with arrow buttons;
  * Journal: tabs;
  * Map;
  * Keypad: large 56×46 keys;
  * Pause: two-column grid;
  * Settings: sliders and switches;
  * Help: topic buttons and text;
  * Dialogs: tap anywhere or "Fortsätt".

## Tutorial (all 10 steps kept)

* All texts are rewritten for touch. Examples:
  * "Använd styrspaken till vänster för att röra dig."
  * "Gå fram till loket och tryck på handlingsknappen nere till höger."
  * "Tryck på kartknappen uppe till höger."
  * "Tryck på Bygg och välj Grundläggande verkstad."
* Visual hints, driven by `GameController.tutorialFocus`:
  * an animated thumb dot with "Dra med tummen här för att gå" over the joystick;
  * a pulsing ring with "Tryck här" around the action button whenever an interaction is possible;
  * pulsing highlights on the map button, then Karta, Kliv av and Bygg in the train bar, the Res hit button, the Build button for the workshop, and the Repair button;
  * a "Svep … Nyp … Tryck på en vagn" line in the train view during the tutorial.
* Story captions sit in the free space between the HUD columns and never take touches.

## Architecture (changes in 0.2)

| Folder | Contents |
|---|---|
| `App/` | `TheLastRailApp` (SwiftUI `WindowGroup`, debug-scenario sandbox) |
| `Core/` | `GameController` (+Flow, +Gameplay), platform-neutral `InputManager` (joystick vector + sprint), `Haptics`, `DebugScenario` |
| `Scenes/` | `SpriteKitView` (`UIViewRepresentable` SKView, multi-touch), `ExplorationScene`, `TrainScene` (UIKit pan/pinch/tap recognizers), `MenuScene` (backgrounds tile to any width) |
| `UI/HUD/` | `TouchControls` (`TouchControlModel`, `TouchControlsView`, `ControlLayout`), `HUDViews` (exploration/train HUD, tracker, tutorial hints) |
| `UI/Panels`, `UI/Screens`, `UI/Components` | Redesigned landscape UI (`PhonePanel`, `CompactPanel`, `IconButton`, `TutorialPulse`) |
| Unchanged | `Models/`, `Systems/` (all rules), `Content/` (stations, recipes, story), `Assets/` (procedural pixel art; colors and images now come from UIKit) |

## Verification performed

* **Builds:**
  * Debug for the iOS Simulator and Release for a generic iOS device (`CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`) both compile with 0 warnings.
  * Xcode 26.4, iOS 26.4 SDK, deployment target iOS 17.
* **Unit tests, 68 of 68 passing** on both iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone SE simulators:
  * all 63 earlier tests (inventory, crafting, travel, tutorial, save/load, content flood-fill and fuel economy, interactions, and both full chapter-1 playthroughs);
  * 5 new `TouchControlTests`:
    * joystick direction and magnitude;
    * **joystick + sprint + action held at the same time**;
    * a second joystick finger is ignored;
    * HUD areas are not claimed by the controls;
    * release-all.
* **UI tests, 6 of 6 passing** on both iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone SE. These use real UIKit touches injected by XCUITest:
  1. Main menu → Nytt spel → dragging the joystick completes tutorial step 1.
  2. Teleport next to the locomotive → the prompt shows → the action button opens the dialog → walking then advances to step 3.
  3. Train swipe and pinch → Karta → tap Rosthamn → Res hit visible → drag the map → depart ("PÅ VÄG").
  4. Device rotated through landscape right, portrait, upside-down and landscape left: the UI stays landscape and buttons stay hittable.
  5. New game → walk → Paus → Huvudmeny → **terminate the app → relaunch** → Fortsätt is enabled → tutorial progress restored.
  6. Depart → arrive at Rosthamn (about 15 s) → Kliv av → the action button boards the train again.
* **Save sandbox:** checked that `save.json` and its backup are in the simulator app container under `Library/Application Support/TheLastRail/`.
* **Visual review** (simulator screenshots via `simctl io`):
  * on iPhone 17 Pro: main menu, depot with tutorial hints, train, map, crafting, inventory, locomotive, a long dialog, the dark mine, travel with a full train;
  * on iPhone SE: depot, full train, map, crafting, inventory, pause, wagons, keypad, tutorial-complete.
  * Fixed from this review: the caption overlapping the tracker, the map legend over station names, and distance labels over names.

## Cannot be verified without a physical device

* **Real multi-touch feel.** XCUITest cannot inject independent simultaneous fingers, so joystick + sprint + action at once is covered by unit tests on the touch model only. Thumb ergonomics, button reach and accidental touches need hands-on play.
* **Frame rate.** The 60 FPS target is configured but not measured on hardware, particularly with rain/snow particles and a long train.
* **Audio and haptics.** The simulator gives no haptics, and audio was not listened to. The silent switch, interruptions (calls) and Bluetooth routing need a device.
* **Dynamic Island / notch on the actual landscape side** (left versus right), and very wide devices (Pro Max). Layout is safe-area based but was only screenshotted on iPhone 17 Pro and SE.
* Total play length and tutorial duration (10–15 min target) on a phone.

## Known limitations

* The built-in Claude Code simulator panel could not be used: it requires `xcode-select` to point at the full Xcode (`sudo xcode-select -s /Volumes/WD-BLACK/User/Apps/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer`), which needs the owner's password. Verification used `simctl` and XCUITest instead.
* Generator, greenhouse and research wagons exist in the data model only ("Ej i version 0.2"). The route to Polaris is a locked teaser.
* No hardware keyboard or game controller support yet (touch only).
* Small in-world text (station signs) is rendered by SpriteKit at the logical resolution and can look soft.
* The project folder is not a Git repository, so no commits were made.

## Next steps (suggested)

1. A playtest on a real iPhone: tune joystick radius and dead zone, button positions, the 0.8× camera, and travel pacing.
2. Game controller support (GameController framework) feeding the existing `InputManager`.
3. Chapter 2: the Polaris route, plus the generator and greenhouse wagons.
4. An optional left-handed layout (mirrored controls) setting.
